name: Teladoc BetterHelp Business
one_liner: BetterHelp online therapy offered through employers and health plans, including Teladoc's Wellbound EAP; same service as BetterHelp.
best_for: People whose employer or health plan offers BetterHelp or Teladoc's Wellbound EAP
Adults with mild to moderate anxiety, depression or stress who want talk therapy from home
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988
People who need intensive or in-person care for severe mental illness
People who don't want their data handled by a company with a recent FTC privacy order
short_description: Teladoc's business channel for BetterHelp: employers, organisations and health plans offer BetterHelp therapy to their people.
long_description: Teladoc Health, which owns BetterHelp, sells BetterHelp's online therapy to employers, organisations, associations and health plans as well as directly to consumers. Teladoc has also launched Wellbound, an employee assistance program for US employer and health plan clients that uses BetterHelp for its counselling, with employee access from January 1, 2026. For a person, the therapy is the same BetterHelp service: matching with a licensed therapist and sessions by video, phone or chat. In 2023 the FTC finalised an order requiring BetterHelp to pay $7.8 million and banning it from sharing health data for advertising, after alleging it had shared email addresses, IP addresses and health questionnaire answers with Facebook, Snapchat, Criteo and Pinterest. This record duplicates the BetterHelp record.
patient_summary: If your employer or health plan offers BetterHelp (for example through Teladoc's Wellbound EAP), you sign up through that benefit and get matched with a licensed therapist for video, phone or chat sessions. Your cost depends on what your sponsor covers. The service is the same as BetterHelp's consumer product.

pricing.starting_price: Through your employer or health plan; cost set by the sponsor
pricing.notes: Sold to employers, organisations and health plans; Wellbound EAP access began January 1, 2026. Without a sponsor, use BetterHelp's consumer subscription.

basis.regulatory_action: FTC order, 2023: $7.8 million and a ban on sharing health data for advertising, after alleged sharing of email addresses, IP addresses and health questionnaire answers with Facebook, Snapchat, Criteo and Pinterest

privacy.notes: Same company and policy as BetterHelp: website data can be shared for ads if you accept ad cookies, and a 2023 FTC order covers past ad sharing of health data.
